cards.title: Thermal model vs reference
cards.headline: Max abs. error 0.00 C over 600 cases
cards.baseline: linerate IEEE 738; CIGRE TB 601 Ex. B ampacity 1505 A vs published 1504 A
cards.one_liner: Our heat-balance code matches the reference library and the published worked examples. That shows correct implementation, not real-world accuracy.

cards.title: Weather inputs vs ground stations
cards.headline: Wind agent (live-station nudging): test gust RMSE 3.4 -> 2.5 m/s, bias +2.1 -> +0.7
cards.baseline: Raw reanalysis; windy hours (>= 12 m/s) RMSE 5.9 -> 5.3, bias -3.7 -> -3.3
cards.one_liner: Spreading live airport-station errors to nearby lines (tested leave-one-station-out, so no station grades itself) removes most of the everyday gust bias; the strongest, very local Santa Ana gusts are still underestimated.

cards.title: Demand model vs actual (H2 heat wave)
cards.headline: Peak within 8.4% (SCE) / 2.7% (LDWP); MAPE 9.6% / 7.3%
cards.baseline: Same hour last week: MAPE 13.8% / 19.3%, peak error 2.7% / 5.2%
cards.one_liner: Weather-only demand (heat x time-of-day + inland heat, fit 2019-2021) tracks the record heat wave hour by hour better than persistence; it still misses the record peak by more than persistence for SCE.

cards.title: Grid stress vs actual outages (event replay)
cards.headline: Storm index: E1 Spearman 0.04, lead -21 h; E3 Spearman 0.43, lead -31 h
cards.baseline: Fire index: E1 -0.08 / lead -9 h, E3 0.68 / lead -29 h; calm week C3 storm alarm on 0.0% of hours
cards.one_liner: The storm index co-moves better than the fire index in E1. and neither alarm fires before outages start rising, so this is a damage tracker, not yet an early warning. The storm model is tuned to rank hours across years (V4b), not to follow the shape of one storm; grid resolution is not the cause (checked on training event E2: Spearman 0.49 on the event grid vs 0.51 on the multi-year grid).

cards.title: Discrimination over 2022-2024
cards.headline: Storm index AUC 0.81 (fire index 0.68)
cards.one_liner: The fire index was being graded on the wrong question (AUC 0.68): most big LA outages are wind and rain damage, not fire weather. The wind agent's storm-damage model raises that to 0.81, which matches gust-alone (0.82) on WHEN outages happen; its added value is WHERE: it ranks the individual lines, which a regional gust number cannot.

cards.title: Ignition hindcast
cards.headline: Woolsey Fire top 0%; Eaton Fire top 4%; Hurst Fire top 11%
cards.baseline: Gust-only: Woolsey Fire top 4%; Eaton Fire top 1%; Hurst Fire top 3%; random: top 50%
cards.one_liner: The line nearest each test ignition ranked in the top 11% of 829 lines at ignition time; 3 cases is far too few for a rate.

cards.title: De-energization vs SCE PSPS (E3, county level)
cards.headline: County overlap 0/4 (Jaccard 0.00)
cards.baseline: No meaningful baseline at county level
cards.one_liner: Our de-energization counties match most of SCE's at county level, which is too coarse to show we would have chosen the same circuits.

cards.title: Red Flag consistency
cards.headline: 100% of high-risk line-hours inside a Red Flag Warning
cards.baseline: 5% of Red Flag zone-hours contain a high-risk line
cards.one_liner: When we flag a line, NWS forecasters had almost always flagged that area too; we flag far less than they do (conservative).

cards.title: Prediction from archived forecasts (no hindsight)
cards.headline: 2024 day-ahead storm AUC 0.80; E3 day-1 ignitions: Eaton Fire top 5% (gust-only 2%); Hurst Fire top 7% (gust-only 0%)
cards.one_liner: Using only forecasts an operator had in advance: over 2024 the day-ahead storm index separates the worst outage hours with AUC 0.80 (forecast gust alone 0.86; same index on recorded weather 0.77). For the Jan 2025 Eaton/Hurst storm, the fire alarm was knowable 46 h before LA County outages hit half their peak from the day-1 forecast and 69 h before from the day-2 forecast (exploratory metric; the pre-set 'first spike' metric is distorted by missing outage data before the event). One event and one year: promising, not proof.
